title: Discovery-client and account-console interactions emit one structured audit event per named interaction
description: The discovery client and the account-console verification (both on TAC-1201) emit exactly one structured audit event per named interaction from the `keycloak.discovery` and `keycloak.account_console` families. Every event carries fields drawn from the fixed allow-list `family` (one of `keycloak.discovery`, `keycloak.account_console`), `outcome`, `reasonClass?`, `realmSlug`, `at`. No event may carry a token value (access token, id token, refresh token, introspection response body), a client secret, a raw claim record, or a substring of any of the above. The audit sink is contributed by the composed observability blueprint (or by a project-authored sink under the same interface); a sink failure logs a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and never masks the underlying refusal. The other keycloak-side surfaces (JWT verifier, introspection client, provider router, sessionInventory, role adapter) each carry their own audit contract on the TAC that owns the surface (REQ-016 through REQ-019); the token-exclusion rule and the sink-failure posture named here apply verbatim to each of them.
rationale: The five TACs each require structured audit events with slightly different fields; without a cross-cutting REQ naming the allow-list and the token-exclusion rule, a reviewer cannot decide whether a new event field is inside the blueprint's contract. The REQ also anchors the sink-failure posture the guide implies but never states at REQ level.
